hypothesis: Eggs are white, so a bright-pixel threshold on grayscale separates them from the background.
method_change: Baseline: grayscale + global Otsu threshold, nothing else
motivation: Simplest possible baseline to measure everything else against.
observations: Macro IoU 0.345, precision 0.38, recall 0.87. Finds eggs but also marks bright backgrounds and a finger; images 20 and 44 almost fully missed (egg not bright).
next_step: E2: HSV threshold (low saturation + high brightness) to drop coloured things like fingers

hypothesis: Eggs are white: low saturation and high brightness. A colour rule should remove coloured background and fingers that plain brightness keeps.
method_change: Replace grayscale Otsu with HSV rule: saturation <= sat_max AND value >= val_min
motivation: E1 had precision 0.38: it marked fingers and coloured background. Saturation separates white from coloured things.
observations: Macro IoU 0.424 (up from 0.345), precision 0.55, recall 0.70. Best sat_max=40, val_min=170. Dim or shadowed eggs (images 39, 20, 119, 44) almost fully missed; white panel behind egg (125) and a finger still marked.
next_step: E3: add morphological opening and closing to remove specks and fill gaps

hypothesis: Opening removes specks and thin bridges (like a finger link); closing fills gaps from dirt and reflections inside eggs.
method_change: Add morphological opening then closing (elliptical kernel) after the E2 colour rule
motivation: E2 masks are ragged, with holes inside eggs and small false specks in the background.
observations: Macro IoU 0.447 (up from 0.424), precision 0.586, recall 0.690. Opening kernel 9 best (largest value tried, so larger not explored); closing hurt in every setting and was dropped. Dim-egg images and white panel image still fail.
next_step: E4: filter blobs by size, border contact and elongation to drop panels, fingers and specks

hypothesis: Backgrounds and fingers form blobs that are large and wrap the image border, or are long and thin; eggs are compact blobs inside the picture.
method_change: Add connected-component blob filter (min size, border contact, aspect ratio) after E3
motivation: E3 still marks a white panel (image 125) and a finger; colour alone cannot tell them from eggs, shape and position can.
observations: Macro IoU 0.492 (up from 0.447), precision 0.688, recall 0.660. Best min_area 2% of image; border-contact filter hurt in every setting (close-up eggs touch the border) so max_edge=1.0 (off). New zero-IoU images 149 and 150 suggest the filter removed their eggs.
next_step: E5: watershed to split touching eggs before the blob filter

hypothesis: Touching eggs form one merged blob that fails the shape filter; splitting them with watershed first lets each egg pass.
method_change: Insert distance-transform watershed (per-blob peaks) between E3 cleaning and the E4 blob filter
motivation: E4 removed some eggs (images 149, 150) likely because merged eggs became one long blob.
observations: Macro IoU 0.442 (worse than E4 0.492), recall dropped to 0.543. Best peak_frac was 0.5, the setting that splits least, suggesting watershed over-splits single eggs and the cut lines remove pixels (not verified).
next_step: E6: images 149/150 lost eggs because blob aspect ratio 2.7-3.6 failed the 2.5 limit; tune max_aspect

hypothesis: Touching eggs form long blobs (aspect 2.7-3.6); the 2.5 limit removed them, so a looser limit recovers them.
method_change: Keep E3 + E4 filter (min area 2%, no border rule); only raise max_aspect
motivation: Diagnosis of images 149 and 150 showed egg blobs removed only by the aspect-ratio check.
observations: Macro IoU 0.496 (E4 was 0.492). max_aspect 3.0 recovered touching-egg blobs (images 149/150). Worst images are dim or shadowed eggs; blue in error maps is mostly egg pixels below the brightness limit.
next_step: Freeze parameters; run one final evaluation on the held-out evaluation set

hypothesis: Video eggs are darker/warmer than the dataset eggs, so the dataset thresholds miss them.
method_change: Video only: retune HSV saturation/brightness limits on 4 frames (oval proxy from manual boxes); opening and blob filter unchanged
motivation: Preview showed missed eggs in about half of the sampled frames (18, 20, 32, 34-40 s).
observations: Looser colour limits recovered some eggs but also marked shirts and pants; colour alone cannot separate eggs from pale or grey clothing.
next_step: V2: restrict to a horizontal tracking zone where eggs were seen and drop oversized blobs

hypothesis: Eggs stay in a horizontal zone and are smaller than clothes; position and size rules remove clothing that colour cannot.
method_change: Video only: V1 colour sweep + tracking zone y=160-440 + max blob size 12% of frame; opening and blob filter as E6
observations: Brightness limit is the key setting (proxy IoU 0.20 at 170 vs 0.44 at 120). Zone + size limit removed shirts/pants, but table still marked at 22-34 s (blobs with brightness 111-163, solidity 0.55-0.79) and one egg missed at 36 s.
next_step: V3: bright core (eggs are brightness >200, table is dimmer) then small grow

hypothesis: Eggs have a bright core (brightness >200); table pieces are dimmer, so a core-based rule drops the table.
method_change: Video only: bright, low-saturation core -> opening -> small dilation -> keep only where loose rule (sat<=100, val>=120) agrees; zone y=160-440; blob filter min 1%, aspect 3.0
motivation: V2 still marked the table (blobs val 111-163, solidity 0.55-0.79) and merged eggs with table.
observations: Bright core (sat<=60, val>=170) + opening + 21 px grow, limited to loose rule (sat<=100, val>=120), zone y=160-440. Proxy IoU 0.554 on 4 boxed frames (V2 0.443); right egg count in 3 of 4 frames; 16-frame preview judged good by visual check.
